requirement:
Under `confirm`, a first `false` MUST finish the round for that subject. After
`true` or FIXME, the harness MUST obtain exactly one independent second assessment
of the same subject, with the same mandatory inputs and source state. Each
assessment may discover additional inputs and has its own usage record under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.authoring.confirmation`. I did not request implementation source, because the tests' inputs and assertions were enough to judge.

**First `false` finishes the round under `confirm`**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[without_confirm_or_after_a_false_judgment_one_assessment_is_recorded]` runs the confirm case with a first `false`. It asserts that exactly one provider request and one usage log exist, and that the recorded rationale is the first one.

**After `true` or FIXME, exactly one second assessment**
- A first `true` is covered by `fn[citation_reviews_are_confirmed_with_fresh_targeted_conversations]`. It asserts a second assessment with its own usage record. Its three prompts are two for the first assessment, because of a line-number correction retry, and one for the second. It asserts two usage logs.
- A first `true` followed by `false` is covered by `fn[structural_assessments_and_confirmation_use_the_same_structural_contract]` and `fn[disagreeing_citation_assessments_record_both_explanations]`. Each asserts exactly 2 prompts, so no third assessment runs.
- A first FIXME is covered by `fn[agreeing_assessments_record_the_first]`. It asserts exactly 2 prompts and 2 usage logs.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_runs_a_second_assessment_with_its_own_usage_record]` runs end to end and asserts exactly two requests for the subject.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_with_all_runs_a_second_assessment_for_each_batch_subject]` asserts that every batch subject gets exactly two assessments.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[policy_comes_from_the_flag_then_the_configuration_then_defaults_to_confirm]` asserts 2 conversations under `confirm` and 1 under `once`.

**Independence**
- In `fn[agreeing_assessments_record_the_first]`, the two conversations are separate and each starts from the initial prompt.
- In the citation test, `prompts[2]` does not contain the first review's text.
- In `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]`, each request has a single input item, and the first assessment's rationale sentinel never appears in a later request.

**Same subject, mandatory inputs and source state**
- `fn[agreeing_assessments_record_the_first]` asserts `prompts[0] == prompts[1]`.
- The structural and citation tests assert that the subject and item are in every prompt.
- No test mutates sources between the two assessments. The requirement does not call for that, so I treat it as an unnamed edge case.

**Each assessment has its own usage record**
- `fn[agreeing_assessments_record_the_first]` asserts two logs, with subjects `requirements.ready` and `requirements.ready (second assessment)`.
- The citation test asserts two logs with different `run_id` values.
- The CLI test asserts both subject names in the usage records.
- The adaptive test asserts distinct run ids per model.

**Out of scope**
- Additional inputs discovered by each assessment are permitted by the text ("may"), so they need no test.
- `src/commands.rs#mod[tests]/fn[status_lists_definitions_and_reviews_whose_assessments_disagreed]` only checks status reporting. It adds no obligation here.

text: :::{req} confirmation
Under `confirm`, a first `false` MUST finish the round for that subject. After
`true` or FIXME, the harness MUST obtain exactly one independent second assessment
of the same subject, with the same mandatory inputs and source state. Each
assessment may discover additional inputs and has its own usage record under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.
:::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
